## R741 — The author's resolution of the splitting obstruction, with the gauge characterization (APPLIED; tree 36 pp; refs clean)
- Author: B + C (intrinsic) is idempotent while the weighted Aethus (B + C)/2 is not; stripping weights from Aethae as coefficients would be a major mistake. My R740 candidate (coefficients moved into the valuation, "event algebra vs measure") RETRACTED and replaced.
- New candidate in the algebra paper (after prop:splitting-obstruction): keep weights as coefficients; change the embedding of carriers — a carrier holding a carving = unit sum of its cells, idempotent in the validity quotient ((B+C)² = B + C + 2BC, BC invalid); the weighted Aethus bB + cC a distinct, generally non-idempotent element. Author's gauge point made exact via the Relational Weight Principle's common-rescaling freedom: over exclusive valid cells, W = Σ w_i C_i (w_i > 0) has W² = λW iff all w_i equal (W² = Σ w_i² C_i, coefficientwise comparison) — idempotents up to gauge = uniformly weighted combinations = rescaled carriers (½B + ½C is A in another gauge); ⅔B + ⅓C squares to ratio 4:1, not idempotent even up to gauge; intrinsic Aethae = gauge classes of idempotent weighted Aethae. Open part stated: grain — with unit-sum carriers a coefficient is a weight per finest cell, so refining B = B1 + B2 gives bB = bB1 + bB2, to be reconciled with share preservation under refinement (the coherence obligation). Note for later: multiplication is well defined on gauge classes (rays), addition needs a common gauge — the RWP's structure; parallel to quantum states as rays.

## R742 — The Relational Weight Principle read at last; the obstruction restated in the quantities it defines (APPLIED; tree 36 pp; refs clean)

The principle (long paper, prince relational_weight_principle, L4494; settled 2025, recorded June 12, 2026): no Aethus is given an absolute scale factor; the defined quantities are weight ratios — the P(A|B) of the weight–probability equivalence — and NEVER bare coefficients; rescaling every Aethus by one positive constant is an exact invariance ("as a logarithmic derivative is blind to a constant multiplicative factor"); "the weight structure is, in a word, projective."

- CANONICAL SPECIFICATION audited against (owner paper in brackets):
  (1) child ≠ proper child: proper child = a visible term of a parent's declared decomposition; P3 quantifies over proper children (an Aethus is its own proper child at weight one) [algebra].
  (2) structural invalidity ≠ zero weight: invalidity fixes admissibility; weights grade within it; a probabilistic representation may put zero weight on forbidden cells, but zero weight alone does not identify invalidity [causality; quantum (S)/(W)].

  (6) structural coefficient ≠ physical probability: coefficient = relative component weight; probability = renormalized weight in the validity quotient; kernel posited, Born statistics represented on a finite domain [algebra; quantum].

- Main text (\textit{Blankness is tense-free.}) replaced by the referee's tighter paragraph; the author's formulation kept ("In the comprehensive development's formulation, \emph{blankness-resolution, not pastness, is the Markovian decider of determinacy}."), consolidated note attached after it, \cite{Aethus} moved to the note's end; "Section~\ref{sec:battery}'s sinkhole case illustrates this distinction." restores the section reference. INTEGRATED FROM MY TREATMENT / THE OLD SECOND NOTE: phenomenology framing as the opening; "jointly invalid" (framework term) for the pruned combinations; learning "by observation or by deduction from the state's content" (the old note's "resolution by deduction counting as learning"); one-clause gloss "``Markovian'' marks just this dependence of determinacy on the indexing state, not a stochastic Markov property" (referee's condition, since the old gloss "the draw has not yet happened" was removed as tense-laden); "To say the state holds both is…" (the bare "Both" had lost its antecedent with "mourner" gone).
- Removed from source per the referee: the commented copy of the author's original note (revision history). Checked: the reopening-vs-settling sentence and the AethusRealist cross-reference live elsewhere in the paper and are untouched.
- AUTHOR'S ORIGINAL NOTE (October 2026), preserved here verbatim since it is no longer in the source:

```
Perhaps the central substance to this proposed ontology is how it changes the basic phenomenology of reality. We can illustrate this with the most extreme of occurrences: having a parent or grandparent who died in a terrorist attack or violent event. Even if this happened years ago, because the past is open the event of it itself remains unresolved in the Markovian sense, relative to you. So the answer to \textit{are you a mourner} is that you are both, one in each branch for whether this ancestor of yours died in the event or lived. Suppose even you have a friend who is fully aware of the event herself—so long as you remain unaware of it, the contents of her own mind exist in superposition relative to you, such that in one “branch” your ancestor died and she is aware of this, and in the other your ancestor lived and she is aware of this. Respectively, that would make you a mourner versus not a mourner. Furthermore, there might be a branch where she is not aware of the event, however if you yourself know just enough to know she was aware of that something but not enough to distinguish whether the ancestor lived or died, then that prunes relative to you the cases where your friend is not aware of the event at all. The point of the matter is that despite out being able to identify these different “branches” through indexing them by a single attribute, still each scenario holds the joint conjunction of many compatible attributes, that way the “friend knows ancestor died” from “ancestor died and friend knows they died” cannot mix with the “ancestor lived” from “ancestor lived and friend knows they lived”. Trivially speaking, the set of all possibilities is indexed by the set of combinations of outcomes, and after pruning the invalid ones we retain the specially coupled conjunctions locking off each branch from one another. Where the framework also becomes especially relayed to quantum mechanics itself is in that the phenomenological “both” of “are you a mourner or not” is truly a disjunction, but under the ontological overhaul of instating partial information states and an open past ultimately becomes the very category of which the “both” from quantum mechanics is an instance. As for your friend themselves, the answer to how and in what way multiple people can coexist in a relative reality is that you get an informational sliver of knowledge about a given event, like what you are aware of in the common football game you are watching, and the friend gets another—then simply put the friend goes into superposition of all possible such slivers relative to you which are not pruned, and to each of their slivers you go into superposition of all possible slivers which do not contradict it (that is, that are not pruned relative to them). Ultimately then there is no single sliver of theirs which coexists with yours, because even they themselves are subject to the same rule of no complete determinacy relative to your information state.
```

## R795 — Golden reasoning: the author's "nuclear equilibrium" idea worked out (new files; no paper touched)
- outputs/golden_nuclear_equilibrium/: two_order_hazard_note.tex (+ .pdf, 5 pp, builds clean), two_order_hazard.py (standard library + matplotlib), the figure.
- The model, in the survivorship/technoanatomy coordinates (technostrength x, anatomy ρ; viability Λ_∞ < ∞): one self-generated lane with a two-state anatomy regime (favorable +, unfavorable −) switching at second-order hazards a (−→+) and b(h) = b₀ + b₁h (+→−, crisis feedback); lane log-hazard dℓ = −m̄(ρ₊1₊ − ρ₋1₋)dt, floored by the global technoanatomic floor γe^{−ρ_G x} and capped at h_max. Mean-field skeleton bistable iff ρ₊a > ρ₋b₀ with separatrix h* = (ρ₊a − ρ₋b₀)/(ρ₋b₁) [P within the model]; negative basin fatal and fast (P(T>t) ≤ e^{−h*(t−t₀)}); positive basin Golden-compatible iff ρ_G > 0 — a positive carrying-capacity floor is fatal on its own (rate γ), so the positive equilibrium buys time, not viability, unless the global anatomy is favorable. Continuous (OU-response) interpolation and the mode classes (basin × sign ρ_G) stated.
- The inference: with C the observer baseline and E the Golden-compatible class of weight w over the counterfactual route Aethus, BF_T(E) = P(G_T|E,C)/P(G_T|C) = 1/(w + (1−w)r_T) ↑ 1/w; the observer hypothesis contributes no factor since E is downstream of C (Substitution Property's upstream-only discipline) — the "post-observer, pre-Golden" discriminator class (coal and the Granicus are members; the nuclear attribute's route-deletion is a theorem of the model rather than case work). Within-model accordance satisfied trivially; the evidence is the between-model Bayes factor (prop:bf form); ceiling 1/P(G_T|C) and no certification (thm:ceiling); predeclaration and multiplicity guard noted. Numerics: at w = 0.25 the Bayes factor saturates at 4 by T ≈ 10 under a ceiling 4.7.
- OPEN, stated in the note: w from a declared route class [O]; the lane's global anatomy sign ρ_G [O/S]; the lane's present basin [S, empirical]; the structural simplifications [S].

## R796 — Golden reasoning: the author's "lanes as technoanatomy modes with soft branches" intuition worked out (new files; no paper touched)
- outputs/golden_nuclear_equilibrium/: resolution_tree_note.tex (+ .pdf, 5 pp, builds clean), resolution_tree.py, the figure. Companion to the two-order note.
- The substrate: a lane = a signature class of hazard events under the record structure; the lane tree = the nesting of signature partitions; h_v = rate of events individuated to exactly v (post-branch; jointness at internal nodes); H_root = Σ_v h_v over the partition, so lanes add only as post-branch hazards over an antichain cut — the no-double-counting lemma [P]. Aethic content: by the Record-Individuation Lemma an event individuated only to the clade has no lane; the lane attribute stands blank over the clade's children (constructive, not epistemic).
- The soft branch: resolution r_i = 1 − exp(−d_i τ h_i) (Poisson arrival of lane-individuating records at a rate ∝ the lane's own hazard), crossover h_× = 1/(d_i τ); stated decomposition stated(h_i) = r_i h_i, stated(h_C) = h_C + Σ(1−r_i)h_i, total unchanged [S].
- Rendering: anatomy acts on stated attributes: d log h_i/dt = −m̄[r_i ρ_i + (1−r_i)ρ_C]. Derived floor [P within the model]: below h_× a lane inherits the clade's response; ρ_C > 0 → continues down integrably; ρ_C = 0 → ḣ = −m̄ρ_i d τ h², power-law stall h ≈ h_×/(m̄ρ_i t), Λ diverges logarithmically (the "knot", informational: nothing stated to act on); ρ_C < 0 → turns up. The first note's γe^{−ρ_G x} is this regime with ρ_G = ρ_C and γ ~ h_×. "Coming online"/eavesdropping: the clade readout h_C + h_2 once lane 1 dissolves; the unresolved lane is estimable only as total minus resolved siblings.
- Numerics (d τ = 10, h_× = 0.1; ρ_1 = 1, ρ_2 = 0.1; h_C(0) = 0.02): lane 1 bends at the crossover and stalls under ρ_C = 0 (h_1(30) = 3.65e-3 vs the formula's 3.3e-3); lane 2's share of the readout rises 0.09 → ~0.5; the naive sum of lane estimates overcounts H_C by 2.7× (ρ_C = 0) and 3.0× (ρ_C = 0.3) at t = 20.

## R797 — Golden reasoning: the pooled lane tree — cross-lane baselines, the pooled no-double-counting law, the exponential as an asymptote (new files; no paper touched)
- outputs/golden_nuclear_equilibrium/: lane_tree_coupling_note.tex (+ .pdf, 5 pp, builds clean), lane_tree_coupling.py, the figure. Third note in the series.
- The pool recursion: P_v = c_v + Σ_{u∈ch(v)} (1−r_u)P_u, r_v = 1 − exp(−d_v τ P_v), r_root = 1; stated S_v = r_v P_v; a lane's baseline B_i = P_pa(i). No-double-counting, pooled form [P]: Σ_v S_v = Σ_v c_v (checked to 1e-16); baselines are aliases, never added.
- The cross-lane filter [P within the model]: ∂B_1/∂c_2 = e^{−dτc_2}(1 − dτc_2): rises below h_×, saturates at h_×/e, falls above (a fully individuated loud sibling withdraws from the pool — a prediction the author did not name); cousins enter through extra (1−r) factors along the path = tree proximity; the baseline is the joint action of the whole structure.
- Effective anatomy: ρ_eff(v) = Σ_k [Π_{j<k}(1−r_{a_j})] r_{a_k} ρ_{a_k} (weights sum to one); d log c_v = −m̄ ρ_eff(v) dt. Feedback: siblings' unresolved content swells the clade pool, raises r_C, raises ρ_C's weight for a quiet lane.
- The separatrix returns from resolution alone [P within the model]: an unfavorable lane (ρ_v < 0) under a favorable parent is carried down iff r_v < r* = ρ_eff(pa)/(ρ_eff(pa) − ρ_v), i.e. c_v < c* = −log(1−r*)/(d_v τ); predicted c* = 0.062 on the example, computed outcomes 0.05 carried down / 0.069 runaway.
- Aggregate [P within the model]: H_int = Σ c_v, mode-wise exponential in x at each node's effective rate; as the structure quiets every ρ_eff → ρ_root, so H_int ~ Γ_eff e^{−ρ_root x} — the companion's internal channel asymptotically with ρ = the global technoanatomy (aggregate rate 0.300 vs ρ_root = 0.3 on the example); viability iff driver viable, ρ_root > 0, and no non-positive node above its separatrix (weakest link).
- OPEN: clade contents as own vs constituted [S]; d_v [O]; stochastic record process (the joint-process form) [S]; the joint model with the first note's regime switching [S, not run].

## R798 — Golden reasoning: the lane tree as an adjoint structure + the stochastic base (fourth note), AND the full mechanism integrated into the Golden master as new §13 "The lane tree" (APPLIED; master 328 pp in the container build (316 before), refcheck OK, 0 undefined refs, 0 errors, overfull count unchanged at 2)
- Fourth note: outputs/golden_nuclear_equilibrium/adjoint_note.tex (+ .pdf, 9 pp, builds clean, no bitmap fonts), adjoint_check.py, stochastic_base.py (+ figure .pdf/.png). Answers the author's fourth question (limiting emergent constraint / adversivity-like stationary structure / potential energy / interplay / structure) and the follow-up on relating the explicit sum of exponentials to the lanes sum and developing H ≈ Γ_eff b^x with stochastic b.
- Adjoint structure [P]: pools = forward absorbing upward walk (absorption prob. r_a at each ancestor, certain at the root); stated amounts = absorbed mass; no-double-counting = conservation. ρ_eff(v) = expected anatomy at absorption = unique solution of the backward equation ρ_eff(v) = r_v ρ_v + (1−r_v) ρ_eff(pa(v)). Duality ⟨ρ_eff, c⟩ = ⟨ρ, S⟩ (0.610193 both, diff 0); dH/dx = −⟨ρ,S⟩ (fd −0.6075 vs −0.6102, gap = step re-evaluation of r). Bilinear action L = Σ c_v φ_v − Σ r_v P_v ρ_v + Σ λ_v(P_v − c_v − Σ_{u∈ch(v)}(1−r_u)P_u): stationarity gives both recursions, φ = λ = ρ_eff (multiplier = effective anatomy; equal at every node), saddle value 0. Stationary point is a saddle (optimal-control adjoint pair), NOT a potential minimum.
- Quiet limit [P]: contents → 0 ⇒ r → 0 below the root ⇒ ρ_eff ≡ ρ_root (A1: 0.557, 0.329, 0.303, 0.300 at contents ×10⁻¹…10⁻⁴; ρ_root = 0.3); ⟨ρ_eff,c⟩ → ρ_root H: the companion's Γe^{−ρx} with ρ = ρ_root. This is the "limiting emergent constraint": a harmonic function with one boundary value.
- Marginal vs average anatomy [P]: ∂⟨ρ,S⟩/∂c_v = λ̃_v = r_vρ_v + (1−r_v)λ̃_pa + r_v'P_v(ρ_v − λ̃_pa) (individuation term); fd agrees to 6 places at every node; averages/marginals: A1 0.995/1.021, A2 0.196/0.139, B1 0.462/0.546. Past the crossover the coefficient g' = 1 − e^{−u}(1−u) > 1, so the marginal can be NEGATIVE with all ρ > 0 (ρ_A2 = 0.02, u = 2: average 0.0525, marginal −0.0084). Potential: exists at frozen resolution (pairing linear; rendering = its multiplicative gradient flow); with responding resolutions none: ∂ρ_eff(A1)/∂c_A2 = −0.00119 vs ∂ρ_eff(A2)/∂c_A1 = +0.00956 (symmetric only at equal u; 0.000139 both at equal contents). Acyclicity remark: frustration/degenerate minima need cycles (the institutional graph); the tree's balance has a unique exact solution.
- The two sums [P]: H = Σ_v c_v(0) exp(−∫ρ_eff(v)) (by origin: the sum of exponentials; the earlier notes' Σ Γ_i e^{−ρ_i x} is its resolved limit r ≡ 1) = Σ_a S_a (by absorption: the lanes sum, jointness counted once at internal nodes); at x = 0 H = 0.790 both ways, internal nodes 12.8%, leaves 87.2%.
- Exact single exponential [P]: d log H/dx = −ρ̂, ρ̂ = Σ_a (S_a/H) ρ_a (stated-share-weighted anatomy), so H = Γ_eff q_x^x EXACTLY with q_x = exp(−(1/x)∫ρ̂) (the author's "b"; in the master written q_x to match Remark sch:rem:internalgates's Γq^x, which thereby gets its referent). min ρ ≤ ρ̂ ≤ max ρ. Drift dρ̂/dx = −Var_c(ρ_eff) + ⟨ρ̇_eff,c⟩/H (selection + resolution drift): −0.1159 = −0.0900 − 0.0250 at x = 0; ρ̂ falls 0.77 → min 0.2955 at x ≈ 8.8 (undershoot: slow lanes still partly resolved) → 0.300.
- Quenched (stochastic) model [P within the model]: each window τ_r, each lane resolves with prob. r_v(P_v) given realized child pools; content renders at the first resolved ancestor's anatomy; the pooled tree is its mean field. 2000 realizations, τ_r = 1: q_x mean/sd 0.6865/0.0173, 0.7142/0.0099, 0.7274/0.0051 at x = 10, 20, 40 (mean field 0.6807, 0.7110, 0.7258; → e^{−0.3} = 0.741): self-averaging. E[H(40)] = 2.43e−6 vs mean field 2.14e−6 (+14%); annealed anatomy 0.317 vs 0.321 (Jensen; the master's "mean carried by branches that patched luckily" made a number). Bimodality at the separatrix (ρ_B1 = −0.3, c* = 0.0539 self-consistent): q_40 quiet mode 0.751 (n = 807) / growing mode 1.221 (n = 1193), mean-field 0.815 in neither; P(grow) = 0.378, 0.597, 0.791 at 0.8c*, c*, 1.25c* (stochastic separatrix slightly below the deterministic). Golden reading [S]: the growing mode is non-viable, so Golden-conditioning selects the quiet mode; "asymptotically or mode-wise" both confirmed in the model; a mechanism for the anatomy selection of §gr:subsub:anatsel.
- Adversivity as boundary data [S]: scope map k(v); ρ_v = β_v(W*_{k(v)}) − α_v(W*_{k(v)}) at scope equilibria of the adversivity energy; the two trees (modes vs agents) NOT identified; distinct equilibria = "distinct setups"; the quiet limit keeps only the top scope's ρ ("top of a flow" with the flow = the backward equation). Political cross-talk [S]: lane contents as the external field in the ledgers (net_i = Σ w_ij s_j − f_i(c)); arrival (10→28 allied pairs, 8 inversions) raises β for sibling modes; removal lowers it slowly; sign-definite, unlike the record coupling (eq. cross), and persistent after the loud lane individuates. Coupled system (7 lines, graded); record loop (acyclic, exactly solvable) vs political loop (cyclic, degenerate); a global potential needs the coordination-cost scaling β [O]; candidate = the pairing at scope equilibria.

## R813 — The Hațeg prior re-estimated from data; the accordance route carried separately on the isolating configuration and on the island's fauna; the forward prediction derived with its premises named; the Montana fossils' status and route; the author's ghost-lineage principle, with his second message of October 13, 2026 quoted verbatim; the round's bibliography in one file (author-directed, Oct 13 2026) (APPLIED; Nexic master 230 pp in the container build, was 228; Optimal Earth 35 pp stubbed and 37 with its real bibliography, was 34 and 36; 0 errors and 0 undefined references in both)
- REQUEST: the author asked five things.
  - Are the Montana fossils confirmed primates? He noted that the falling sea level after the extinction makes the dispersal plausible.
  - Answer "nothing primate-like has been found on Hațeg" with his principle that the ancestors of later major clades are obscure in their own time.
  - Redo his 6% model with better data or statistics.
  - Does the paper unpack the forward inference, that something major in the Cenozoic required our ancestors to be arboreal at the boundary? ("Make sure you think before you impulsively hedge!")
  - Quote that message as a verbatim footnote.
  Mid-turn he also asked for one file with the newest bibtex for the two papers.
- THE RE-ESTIMATE (supplementary script hateg_prior.py; numpy only, fixed seed; its printed output is delivered beside it and reproduces).
  - The single example's colonization model is kept. Its even split is replaced by measured shares:
    - formidable theropods among large-dinosaur genera in nine Campanian–Maastrichtian mainland assemblages, 18/99 = 0.18;
    - land predators among large over-water colonists of 27 long-isolated Cenozoic islands, 12/77 = 0.16;
    - all predators including the semi-aquatic Crocodylus, 24/89 = 0.27;
    - mammalian carnivores alone, 3/68 = 0.04.
    The model uses four to seven herbivorous colonizations, Beta posteriors and a Gamma–Poisson check.
  - Result: P(no formidable theropod | isolated island) is 0.33 (90%: 0.16–0.52) on the source-fauna share and 0.39 (0.19–0.60) on the land-predator share. Across the four readings the medians run 0.18–0.75. That is about one in three, five to six times the single example's 6.25%. Island area, which the model omits, would raise these figures (Burness et al. 2001).
  - The fluke is relocated, not removed. What was rare is the isolation's persistence. The sea-level surrogate test prices the Late Cretaceous configuration (LC) at 0.0134 per realization at the window's exact extremes and 0.045 at the canonical tolerance. Taking it as the price of Hațeg's isolation is a proxy, stated as such. On the least favourable settings of tab:sealevel-robustness at which the test still separates the window (the 2–25 band and the quarter-sd tolerance) it is about 0.11.
  - Stage one, run separately on the two parts:
    - the configuration: floor 0.91–0.97 at κ = 1 and 0.69–0.90 at κ = 4; still 0.78 and 0.34 at P_LC ≈ 0.11;
    - the island's fauna given LC: floor 0.23–0.34 at κ = 1, none at κ = 4;
    - the composite: probability 0.005–0.017, but its floor is the configuration's, and the text says it adds nothing locally.

    - the shared premises of the two routes stated.

## R814 — The Hațeg prior rebuilt on lineage arrivals, at the author's correction; the refuge's joint price carried into the forward argument; the discharge of the arboreal requirement; the superclades on the island and their exits; the genetic-over-fossil position stated explicitly; the purgatoriids' placement not assumed (author-directed, Oct 13 2026) (APPLIED; Nexic master 233 pp in the container build, was 230; Optimal Earth 36 pp stubbed and 38 with its real bibliography, was 35 and 37; 0 errors and 0 undefined references in both)
- REQUEST: the author rejected R813's share-based re-estimate as statistically naive.
  - The random variable is whether a formidable-theropod lineage EVER reached the island over its ~30 Myr life while several other clades did. A lineage that arrived would have radiated, so species or genus proportions are irrelevant.
  - His premise: whatever let the herbivore clades across let the carnivores across, all conditional on no sea-level drop.
  - He asked for:
    - the joint probability with the sea-level configuration, for the Cenozoic conditioning argument;
    - his full nuance carried over, including the paper's siding with genetic over fossil evidence and the ontology that goes with it, cross-referenced to the Nexic packaging argument as an explicit philosophical position;
    - the inference of what the arboreal necessity could be (its Nexic discharge);
    - the superclades reconstructed to their Cretaceous locations, as he did for rodents ("the whole system");
    - no in-paper assumption that the purgatoriids are primates. He passed on a Gemini note saying the evidence is not overwhelming, and his own skepticism given how rare Cretaceous placental fossils are.
  - Mid-turn he added: if they are stem primates, their rapid spread fits a head start. He also asked for his "blast and sifting" thesis to be included: island populations, spared the mainland's post-extinction competition, entered the mainland with larger populations when the land bridge formed.
- THE MODEL (hateg_prior.py, version 2; numpy only, deterministic grid integration; the output file is delivered beside it and reproduces).
  - Each lineage class of the archipelago reaches the island in a Poisson process while it is present there. The outcome per class is binary.
  - The window runs from the island's emergence (93.9 Ma) to the end of its dated record (about 67.0 Ma).
  - On the author's premise, one rate serves the comparable lineages and the predators alike.
  - Calibration: the archipelago's non-volant dinosaur lineages of medium or large size (census from Csiki-Sava et al. 2015, ZooKeys 469).
    - Reached: titanosaurs, nodosaurids, rhabdodontids, non-hadrosaurid hadrosauroids (exposures 26.9, 26.9, 18.7, 16.6 Myr).
    - Not reached: lambeosaurines (3.0) and the giant flightless birds (8.0).
  - Prediction: the medium-sized abelisaurids.
    - Conservative reading: from Tarascosaurus, early Campanian, 3–4 m (Ősi & Buffetaut 2011).
    - Fuller reading: from the Cenomanian (Caletodraco, Buffetaut et al. 2024).
    - The Santonian Iharkút abelisaurid, about 1.8 m, is outside the class.
  - The prior is log-uniform on the rate.
- RESULTS: P(no formidable lineage established during the documented interval | isolation):
  - 0.13 on the fuller reading and 0.29 on the conservative one.
  - With the tetanurans counted, if an island population would have outlived its source: 0.09 and 0.18.
  - Uniform prior, fuller reading: 0.06.
  - Lineage-level counting on both sides: 0.09–0.14 and 0.18–0.26, depending on the lirainosaurines' exposure.
  - Weakened premise:
    - the distance reading leaves no medium-sized formidable lineage in the east during the documented interval, so the absence was expected;
    - all non-volant tetrapod lineages: 0.48.
  - Premise check: on Cenozoic islands, measured exactly as here, 4 of the 6 islands with four or more herbivore lineages never received a terrestrial predator.
  - Joint with the sea-level configuration: 0.0017–0.0056 (fuller) and 0.0038–0.0127 (conservative); up to 0.031 on the least favourable separating settings.
  - Stage-one local floor at κ=1: 0.75 (fuller) and 0.43 (conservative); at κ=4, 0.27 and none.
  - Forward factors at κ=1: 1/180–1/600 (fuller), 1/80–1/260 (conservative), 1/30–1/70 (least favourable sea-level settings); 1/20–1/75 for the configuration alone.
  - The R813 share-based estimate (one in three) is withdrawn in the text.
- NEXIC master:

## R815 — The Hațeg prior rebuilt on the author's species draw; the author's classification of the formidable class; the refuge's horizon carried to the boundary; two errors in R814's census corrected (author-directed, Oct 14 2026) (APPLIED; Nexic master 234 pp in the container build, was 233, and 239 with its embedded bibliography through bibtex, was 238; Optimal Earth 36 pp stubbed and 38 with its real bibliography, unchanged; 0 errors and 0 undefined references in both; overfull boxes: Nexic 47, was 49, none new; Optimal Earth 3, unchanged)
- REQUEST, two messages of Oct 14, 2026, verbatim. The first is quoted as the session summary preserved it.
  - (1) "By the way I would definitely count a middle sized theropod of a dromeosaur or something a formidable theropod any day, especially because it would very likely wipe out the early stem primates anyway! What I would NOT count as a formidable theropod is Balaur, because it would have had to have had flying ancestors so as to reach the island in the first place, which I assume wipes out the formidable trait! So yeah by the way does your Poisson statistical model basically look at all the separate non-flying clades which reached there (including ones at the very end, because theropods could have slipped in then too), therefore estimate a statistical range for the lambda in time rate for each based on that count, and then maybe do something like assume there's a broader lambda which then gets a Bernoulli weighted coin flip for herbivore or carnivore when it fires, and then condition that statistical fit lambda we see on the no-carnivore case and try to extrapolate the total lambda for carnivores now? That's what I would do, I think!"
  - (2) "Technically though the Bernoulli coin flip is a projection of a random draw from the set of all species that were around to reach the island, y'know? So repeats of the same species or genus seems very unlikely to me, because even if they're in the same wider clade we'll realize the distinction it from the fossils. So that should be the model—write it so that you have the overarching lambda rate function, then run the species draw when it fires, (which is effectively like splitting to many lambda rates when you decompose it), then conditioning on no theropods (except for flying animals, who have a different rate anyway so they don't count) you fit the lambda rate at a range which produces the empirically seen number of lineages that got there, and then you calculate what the theropod lambda would have been based on its species count!"
- THE MODEL (hateg_prior.py, version 3; numpy only, deterministic; the output file reproduces and every figure the papers quote from it is printed).
  - An overall rate Lambda(t) = c g(t). Each firing draws one species from the pool then living outside the island, so each species has rate Lambda/N while it lives.
  - k is the number of non-formidable arrivals, the lineages the island's fossils distinguish. c is fitted to k. The predators' rate is the formidable share of the pool times Lambda.
  - With a scale-invariant prior on c: P0 = (1 + F_f/F_n)^(-k) exactly. A uniform prior gives exponent -(k+1). A steady composition gives (1-f)^k, of which the single example's (1/2)^4 is the case f = 1/2, k = 4.
  - The absence is not used as data (it is the attribute being priced). By Poisson thinning, conditioning on it leaves the other arrivals' likelihood unchanged. The reading that fits Lambda with the absence among the data gives (1+f)^(-k) = 0.22; the paper says why it is set aside.
  - Repeats: rare if the true pool is several times the census, as the author takes it to be. On a census-sized pool, 8 draws would repeat with probability 0.68, and the occupancy-corrected figure is 0.12; the paper states this.
  - Checked by grid integration against the closed form (0.1582 = 0.1582).
- THE ISLAND'S ARRIVALS: k = 8 (dinosaurs of medium or large size, giant flightless birds included).
  - Three titanosaur lineages (Díez Díaz et al. 2025: near Saltasauridae; with Lognkosauria; near early-diverging South American eutitanosaurs).
  - Struthiosaurus.
  - The telmatosaurids, Telmatosaurus with Kryptohadros (Magyar et al. 2026, JSP 24: 2607800).
  - Transylvanosaurus (Augustin et al. 2022, JVP 42: e2133610).
  - Ferenceratops, with Zalmoxes robustus counted alongside (Maidment et al. 2026, Nature 651: 397–403).
  - Gargantuavis (Mayr et al. 2020, Cret. Res. 106: 104271; disputed by Buffetaut & Angst 2020, Cret. Res. 112: 104438).
  - Alternative counts: 6 by class; 9 with Z. robustus as an iguanodontian; 11 with Uriash and Kryptohadros apart; 7 if Gargantuavis flew in.
- THE POOL (outside the Transylvanian landmass; Santonian to the record's end, about 67.0 Ma; adults about 2 m or more; body fossils only).
  - Two counts, applied to both sides alike:
    - NAMED: 1 formidable species (Arcovenator), 2 with the contested Tarascosaurus, against 19 others: f = 0.05 (0.10).
    - FORMS: named species, plus one form per clade × stage × island cell that only indeterminate records occupy, plus records their describers distinguish. This gives 7 formidable forms against 27 others: f = 7/34 = 0.21.
  - The seven formidable forms:
    - Iharkút early-branching tetanurans;
    - their like at Muthmannsdorf;
    - Tarascosaurus;
    - Arcovenator;
    - the Lo Hueco medium abelisauroid;
    - Taveiro's large tetanuran teeth;
    - the late-Maastrichtian medium abelisaurids.
  - Sources: Fondevilla et al. 2019 (ESR 191: 168–189), Malafaia et al. 2023 (Diversity 15: 141), Ősi & Prondvai 2013 (Cret. Res. 44: 58–63), Tortosa et al. 2014, CS15, and the species' descriptions. The script lists every record with its stage, island and source.
  - A subagent compiled the first census; I checked the key items myself.
- RESULTS, P(A | isolation):
  - Main: (27/34)^8 = 0.16.
  - Named species alone: 0.45 (with Tarascosaurus) and 0.66 (without).
  - Variants:
    - 0.25 (k = 6), 0.20 (k = 7), 0.13 (k = 9), 0.08 (k = 11);

  - Fitted Lambda: 0.36/Myr (90% 0.19–0.62) over 93.9–67.0 Ma. The predators' rate is 0.07/Myr. P0 is 0.36 to 0.03 across the fit's range.
  - Reaching 1/16 needs f = 0.29 at k = 8.

- HULL 2015, READ (the Yale-hosted copy; ScienceDirect is robots-disallowed):
  - What it says: a mass extinction is "a step into a prolonged alternative global ecosystem state"; "strange ecosystems dominate for up to millions of years in their aftermath"; "Rapid evolution in a world emptied of ecological incumbents is expected".
  - What it does not say: it does not describe two waves of losses. The second wave, losses among the event's survivors, is Jablonski 2002's "dead clade walking" (PNAS 99: 8139–8144), checked against the University of Chicago release only: lineages that survived the largest extinctions and died "within the first five or 10 million years thereafter"; "a 17 percent extinction rate for orders following three of the five big mass extinctions".
  - Its caution, added at the forward prediction in both papers: in phylogenies of living lineages neither the EOT nor the K-Pg stands out as changing the rate of evolution in the lineages leading to extant mammals (the Early Eocene Climate Optimum, ~52–50 Ma, does), and "Does the unique selective regime ... in the aftermath really matter for macroevolution? This is a question for future studies to address."
  - The Nexic text now gives Hull for the prolonged aftermath and Jablonski for the second wave ("some of the clades that survived the event itself died out within the next five to ten million years"), "the blast and then the sifting, in the author's terms"; the author's footnote citation becomes Hull and Jablonski, with an EDITED comment keeping the original.
- THE FORMIDABLE CLASS, AT THE DEFINITION:
  - Remark 9, "The Cenozoic test" (label rem:cenozoic-test), follows Definition 17 (Threatening Dinosaurs). It states his test in his terms; his account that it is the full, abstract definition, drawn from the Dark Era and the accordance principle's discharge inference, with the Aethic modality of the K-Pg extinction wired to it; the Aethus-invariance, tied to his own argument just above the Definition (the non-avian category's circularity); the birds as the one clade for which the test ran, with Definition 18 placing them outside the class and the test reaching the same verdict; detours ruining the trait for good, on his view, the volant case argued in sec:hat-objections; his bet on troodontids, dromaeosaurids and tyrannosaurs; and the Hațeg special case, which can inherit the general class's breakages. It cites the verbatim chain (footnote 76, label fn:hateg-chain) and the Hațeg sections.
  - Cross-referenced from: the 6% footnote at the conjecture; the attribute paragraph of the accordance route; the prior section; Optimal Earth's fluke paragraph and its application table.
- THE ISLAND'S THEROPOD RECORD, READING BY READING (the modality pass; latest readings found this round marked NEW):
  - Isolated teeth referred to velociraptorine dromaeosaurids (Csiki & Grigorescu 1998; Smith et al. 2002).

  - Teeth of the Richardoestesia and Paronychodon kinds (Malafaia et al. 2023), form taxa whose families are unsettled; Torices et al. 2015 questioned Paronychodon's place among the troodontids (as Sellés et al. 2021 report).
  - NEW: a Maastrichtian tooth from the NVS site near Vălioara referred to Paraves indet. 1 (Ősi, Kolláti & Nagy 2025).
  - Elopteryx (femora) and the tibiotarsi (Bradycneme, Heptasteornis): a bird (Andrews); the tibiotarsi first referred to Elopteryx, then giant owls (Harrison & Walker 1975); troodontid referrals by several authors, with "little supporting evidence" (Kessler et al. 2005), which Sellés et al. report later work ruled out; most probably a dromaeosaurid (Le Loeuff et al. 1992, as reported by Kessler et al.); a derived maniraptoran and the tibiotarsi a non-maniraptoran tetanuran (Csiki & Grigorescu 1998); possibly a troodontid or a pygostylian bird, Heptasteornis an alvarezsaurid, Bradycneme an indeterminate maniraptoran (Naish & Dyke 2004); most probably a derived maniraptoran reminiscent of the alvarezsaurids (Kessler et al. 2005); a clade with Gargantuavis and Balaur (Mayr et al. 2020); NEW, the latest: a paravian and avialan, "a secondarily flightless bird", Bradycneme its junior synonym, Heptasteornis an alvarezsaurid, and "very possible" synonymy of Elopteryx, Balaur and Mayr et al.'s Nălaț-Vad pelvis (Stoicescu et al. 2024).
  - NEW, a correction: FGGUB R.351, the distal bone R815 and R816's first pass gave as a femur that "may represent a small abelisaurid", "if not avialian" (Csiki & Grigorescu 1998), was read by Kessler, Grigorescu and Csiki (2005) as "the distal end of a moderately large metatarsal, belonging probably to a hadrosaur". On its describers' latest reading it is not a theropod record.
  - Balaur: a predatory dromaeosaurid (Csiki et al. 2010; Brusatte et al. 2013), a flightless avialan (Cau et al. 2015), possibly the same animal as Elopteryx (Mayr et al. 2020; Stoicescu et al. 2024).
  - The Nălaț-Vad vertebra: a middle-sized theropod on its describers' reading (Smith et al. 2002); a possible medium-sized taxon (CS15); an indeterminate medium-sized taxon (Malafaia et al. 2023), perhaps the same.
  - The author's question, "isn't it contested whether those fossils even are them or not?": yes. The island's troodontid evidence is teeth called troodontid-like, and referrals of the femora and tibiotarsi that their critics found poorly supported; Sellés et al. (2021) say troodontid presence in Europe "has been debated for a long time" because "its record was entirely based on isolated teeth", until Tamarro (latest Maastrichtian, Spain). (The first referee quoted "fragmentary, yet controversial" from Sellés et al.; the phrase is not in the paper, only "controversial" in a reference title.)
- THE BET, STATED:
  - On the readings as a dromaeosaurid or a troodontid (and, in Optimal Earth, a non-maniraptoran tetanuran), and on any reading of the vertebra but a detour lineage's, A is false. A stands only on the author's bet that these fossils will prove avian.
  - The author counts a middle-sized theropod of a dromaeosaur's kind as formidable, so pricing A needs the vertebra in a detour lineage too; the papers say that extending the bet to it is the estimate's assumption, not his.
  - The main figure reads Heptasteornis as the bet does (a flier); on its latest readings it is an alvarezsaurid, a non-volant arrival outside the class, and k = 9 gives 0.045. Both papers say so.

- THE CENSUS (hateg_prior.py, version 3.1; numpy only, deterministic; output reproduced byte for byte):

Arcovenator of lower C29r merged into the late-Maastrichtian abelisaurid form. Teeth referred only to Paraves indet., and form taxa of undetermined family, are left out on both sides.

- THE CONCEPT. kappa_q = max(1, q/(1-q)); the canonical variable V = kappa_U * o, U uniform, o the prior odds (drawn from the prior's confidence distribution, independently of U, when the prior is uncertain): the principle's bound read at a random percentile of the realization. In the author's orientation the canonical quantile of a value c is Pr[V > c], falling as c rises, and the canonical ratio at canonical quantile q is the least c with Pr[V > c] <= q (1/r_q is the q-quantile of the canonical cut 1/V), falling as q rises: a higher canonical quantile asks more of the realized side, and the claim at canonical quantile q is carried at level 1 - q. The first pass of the day had the scale the other way (Pr[V <= c]); the author's second message reoriented it; the figures did not change, only the labels.
- THE LONG PAPER. Definition def:canonical-quantiles and Proposition prop:canonical-scale with proof, after Lemma lem:level-reading: (i) for a given prior the canonical quantile of c is o/(c+o) = 1/(1+kappa_c) for c >= o and 1 below, one minus the level lambda_c; r_q = kappa_(1-q) o; Pr[r > r_q] <= q for q <= 1/2 fixed in advance (strict at 1/2); (ii) on the accordance ratio r_q/o = kappa_(1-q) for every attribute, the canonical quantile being Table tab:kappa-scale's failure probability; (iii) under a confidence distribution, one minus the averaged level, the claim at q carried at confidence-weighted level 1 - q, not a guarantee at the unknown prior; (iv) the two-percentile bound kappa_beta o(P_gamma) lies at canonical quantile at most 1 - beta*gamma. A remark: the factor one sits at canonical quantile P(A); above one half a point prior gives the median's bound and an uncertain prior's quantiles come from its spread alone. The percentile paragraph and Table tab:kappa-scale's caption point to the definition.

## R843 (Oct 22 2026, Opus 5.5): the referee's third report on Optimal Earth; the strong canonical scale

- REQUEST. The author: "Here's the referee response to this by the way! And also maybe we try incorporating into various things a strong accordance principle-counterpart canonical ratio column or something for the canonical percentiles/quantiles, like the existing plain accordance principle-based column??? The report: attachment e30eff0b (pasted Oct 22 2026, 20:09), on Optimal Earth as delivered in R842b.
- THE STRONG CANONICAL SCALE. From the full form of Strong Accordance, Pr[canonical ratio >= kappa o] <= log10(1 + 1/kappa)/M for every kappa > 0, with o the realized side's prior odds: at kappa_S(q) = 1/(10^(qM) - 1), log10(1 + 1/kappa) = qM, so the strong canonical bound at canonical quantile q is o/(10^(qM) - 1), log10(10^(qM) - 1) orders of magnitude below the prior odds, about qM once qM exceeds one, each percentage point buying M/100 orders. It has no plateau, the strong form licensing kappa < 1, and it is at or below the plain canonical bound kappa(1 - q) o at every canonical quantile exactly when M >= log10 4 = 0.602 (the threshold is -log10(1 - q)/q below one half, rising, and log10(2)/q above, falling; both equal log10 4 at q = 1/2). The strong envelope K_S = 1/(10^(WM) - 1), W uniform, has Pr[K_S > kappa] = min{1, log10(1 + 1/kappa)/M}; with the prior known only through a confidence distribution, V_S = K_S o is read as V is, the two laws kept apart. M is not estimated for the Hațeg attributes: the columns use M = 10, the long paper's landing-depth value at depths of tens of orders with independent costs (sec:nx-landing-depths, tab:nx-landing-M), as an illustration only.
